articles.title: Ronald Acuña Jr. leaves Tuesday's game early after fouling ball off his left leg
articles.summary: Acuña's injury could impact his availability for the Braves' first playoff series next week.
articles.body:
Ronald Acuña Jr. was unable to finish Tuesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds .

In the bottom of the third inning, the Atlanta Braves star fouled off a pitch that struck the inside of his left leg.

The outfielder looked like he was trying to walk it off, but he couldn't get past it and went down on the field. A trainer came out, and it looked like Acuña was in a lot of pain. He left the field, was pulled from the game, and was replaced by Brewer Hicklen .

Acuña missed time earlier this season due to a hamstring strain. He initially sustained the injury in May and then aggravated it again in early June. This caused him to miss more than a month and a half of action, and he didn't return until July 27.

The good news is that the Braves have already clinched both a postseason berth and the National League East title. The bad news is that if this injury is serious enough that Acuña needs to be added to the IL, any stint would affect his availability for Atlanta's first playoff series.

If Acuña is indeed sidelined for part of the Braves' playoff run, it would not be the first time he has missed out. The outfielder tore his right ACL in July 2021, months before the Braves went on to win the World Series over the Houston Astros .

The 28-year-old is the face of Atlanta's lineup, serving as the leadoff hitter. This season, he has played in 103 games and is slashing /.260/.352/.463 with 20 home runs, 55 RBI, and 20 stolen bases.

Acuña is three years removed from a dominant 2023 campaign where he tallied 41 home runs and 73 stolen bases for the first 40-70 season in MLB history.

The Braves have five more regular season games before the playoffs begin next week. If Acuña is sidelined, Atlanta will have to shuffle around its lineup, likely playing catchers Drake Baldwin and Sean Murphy in the same lineup with one as the DH. This would free up Mike Yastrzemski to take over in right field, but the Braves could also go with Hicklen or Dominic Smith as well.

articles.title: Drew Rasmussen Makes History, Final Box Score Stats & Highlights as Rays Clinch AL East vs. Yankees
articles.summary: As the end of the regular season nears, Drew Rasmussen looks postseason-ready.
articles.body:
As the end of the regular season nears, Drew Rasmussen looks postseason-ready.

The Tampa Bay Rays star pitcher was dealing against the New York Yankees, picking up 11 strikeouts and carrying a no-hitter into the seventh before coming out.

Rasmussen helped the Rays win the American League East and clinch the AL's No. 1 seed as Tampa Bay went on to beat New York 6-1.

Those who have followed the Rays this season are hardly surprised by Rasmussen's showing on Tuesday. The 31-year-old has put together a career season, coming into the matchup with the Yankees with a 15-5 record, a 2.72 ERA and a 0.93 WHIP, along with 163 strikeouts, a career high by more than 30.

If it weren't for Cam Schlittler's outstanding campaign, Rasmussen would very likely be a frontrunner for the AL Cy Young Award.

Rasmussen started his career with the Milwaukee Brewers but has flourished since joining the Rays and becoming an everyday starter, earning his first All-Star nod last year and another one this season.

Behind Rasmussen's tremendous campaign, the Rays are closing in on winning their first divisional title since 2021. Tampa Bay currently sits atop the AL East at 95-61, five games ahead of the second-placed Yankees. A win over New York on Tuesday would clinch the division.

If Rasmussen can keep his momentum going into the postseason, the Rays very well could make a run at the World Series. They also have another star in the rotation in Nick Martinez, who has a 2.94 ERA and 1.07 WHIP. Those two aces make Tampa Bay one of the scariest teams to face for opposing offenses.

articles.title: Rays ride small ball, Drew Rasmussen gem past Yankees to secure AL East, No. 1 seed
articles.summary: Nobody's catching the Rays, who are off to celebrate the AL East title and clinching the AL's No. 1 seed in the visitor's clubhouse at Yankee Stadium.
articles.body:
With the AL East title on the line Tuesday, the Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees offered up a pitchers' duel.

Drew Rasmussen did his part with 6 2/3 one-hit innings to lead the Rays to a 6-1 win over Max Fried and the Yankees . With the victory, the Rays clinched the AL East and sent the Yankees to the wild-card round, where New York is planning to play without Aaron Judge .

The Rays also clinched the No. 1 seed and home-field advantage throughout the American League playoffs. Whoever wins the AL Central and AL West can't catch Tampa Bay , which improved to 96-61, far and away the best record in the AL.

The Yankees — at 90-67 with the loss — are the second team in the AL standings. They're relegated to the wild-card round, but they're locked into the No. 4 seed and home-field advantage once there, thanks to a win over the Rays in the first game of Tuesday's doubleheader.

Rasmussen delivers with division on the line

Rasmussen had dominated the Yankees in four career starts at Yankee Stadium prior to Tuesday, with a 0.72 ERA and 0.80 WHIP in 25 innings. He brought more of the same his fifth time out.

Rasmussen set the tone early by striking out the first three hitters he faced.

Rasmussen's signature cutter repeatedly perplexed Yankees hitters and accounted for strike-3 on seven of his 11 strikeouts. New York didn't log a hit off Rasmussen until a leadoff double by Heliot Ramos in the top of the seventh.

Rasmussen got two more outs before a walk of Jazz Chisholm ended his night. Rays manager Kevin Cash pulled him one out short of finishing the seventh due to Rasmussen's career-high pitch count of 114. Ramos came around to score, but the Yankees failed to mount a threat from there.

When it was done, Rasmussen had secured a line to remember, with 1 hit, 3 walks, 1 earned run and 11 strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings on the night Tampa Bay clinched the AL East over the rival Yankees.

Small ball gets the job done again for Tampa Bay

Tampa Bay's offense did its part in typical Tampa Bay fashion, with small ball and smart baserunning.

After an infield single and a walk to lead off the top of the third inning, Taylor Walls and Cedric Mullins both tagged up on a Yandy Diaz fly ball to put runners on second and third with one out. That allowed Walls to score on a Ryan Vilade ground ball that otherwise could've resulted in an inning-ending double play.

In the seventh, the Rays added insurance with a safety squeeze. Chandler Simpson tagged up to third base on a Nick Fortes fly ball, then scored on a bunt by Walls, who reached first when the Yankees failed to cover the base.

It was the type of thoughtful, efficient offense that Tampa Bay hopes to ride through the playoffs to a World Series title.

The Rays tacked on four insurance runs that weren't necessary, thanks to Rasmussen's gem. When All-Star closer Bryan Baker finished off the Yankees in the ninth, the Rays were off to pop champagne in the visitor's clubhouse at Yankee Stadium.

articles.title: Don Mattingly's Phillies Future Discussed by Dave Dombrowski After Chad Tracy, Andy Green Contracts
articles.summary: Philadelphia Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski weighed in on interim manager Don Mattingly's role after the 2026 season on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski weighed in on interim manager Don Mattingly's role after the 2026 season on Tuesday.

"[We] have felt it is better to wait until our season is complete," Dombrowski told Scott Lauber of The Philadelphia Inquirer (h/t Anthony Franco of MLB Trade Rumors).

Dombrowski also revealed that "there has not been" any additional discussion surrounding Mattingly's future after other recent extensions, via Lauber.

Red Sox Interim Manager Gets Full-Time Job

Earlier on Tuesday, the Boston Red Sox announced that the team was promoting Chad Tracy to a full-time manager position and removing his interim tag. The Red Sox signed Tracy to a contract through the 2029 season.

The New York Mets also removed Andy Green's interim tag and named him full-time manager on Tuesday. Green received a three-year deal from New York as well.

Mattingly is now the only current interim manager in MLB, holding the position since Rob Thomson was fired on April 28.

Philadelphia was just 9-19 at the time, although the team has gone 78-51 since.

It's worth noting the Phillies announced that Mattingly would only remain in his current role through the end of the 2026 season after parting ways with Thomson, although Mattingly has expressed a desire to continue serving in the manager role moving forward.

The 65-year-old has previously operated as a manager of the Los Angeles Dodgers and Miami Marlins, compiling an 889-950 record across 12 years with both clubs.

It appears as though Philadelphia's postseason result will have an impact on Dombrowski's final decision regarding Mattingly, as the Phillies currently hold the final National League Wild Card spot.

articles.title: Ranking MLB's 10 Greatest Postseason Runs Since 2000
articles.summary: A Major League Baseball season unfolds over many months, but one in particular is where memories are made. If you're in the game and you want to become a legend, do it in October.
articles.body:
A Major League Baseball season unfolds over many months, but one in particular is where memories are made. If you're in the game and you want to become a legend, do it in October.

For a reminder of how it's done, let's look back at the 10 greatest playoff runs of the last 25 years.

This could have been a purely objective exercise based on wins, losses and run differential, but that would have risked missing the point. It's better to get subjective for the sake of really getting down to World Series winners that still have "Remember that team?" energy.

To keep things nice and fair, we limited selections to one team per franchise. The teams that made the cut are ranked according to how memorable they are and are likely to remain for years to come.

Was the 2005 White Sox's World Series really that memorable? Truth be told, the best answer is "Eh..." and one of those rocking hand gestures.

However, we simply refuse to participate in the long-running erasure of the 2005 White Sox from our collective cultural memory. They also get style points for A) winning the franchise's first title in 88 years and B) being one of the most dominant teams in history.

The White Sox were never not in first place in the AL Central as they won 99 games in the 2005 regular season. And in MLB's wild card era, only the 2005 White Sox and the 1999 Yankees have pulled off a .900 winning percentage in the postseason.

Pitching guided the White Sox's way that October, wherein 11 of the 12 starts they got resulted in at least 7.0 innings pitched. Altogether, the staff allowed just nine earned runs over 113.0 innings for a 2.55 ERA.

Even if it was a sweep, the White Sox's win over Houston in the World Series was still a white-knuckle experience. Each game was decided by two or fewer runs, and Game 3 lasted 14 innings. We'd also be remiss if we didn't mention Scott Podsednik, he of the zero regular-season homers, walking off Game 2 with a solo shot.

World Series: 4-3 vs. San Francisco Giants

The Angels had existed for 40 years before 2002, and had never once even made the World Series. If you want to know what that kind of agony feels like, only Seattle Mariners fans can tell you about it these days.

If you weren't there for it, trust us when we tell you that the 2002 Angels were one of the great vibes teams anyone had ever seen. The Thunderstix and the Rally Monkey eventually got played out, but it was revolutionary stuff 24 years ago.

The Troy Glaus-Garrett Anderson duo in the lineup was fun. The Troy Percival-Francisco Rodriguez duo in the bullpen might have been even more fun. Mike Scioscia also really liked his small ball , which gave the Angels a different flavor than every other team that October.

Further, the Angels got in everyone's good graces when they knocked the Yankees off in the ALDS. Obviously not Yankees fans' good graces, mind you, but everyone else was sick of the Yankees after they had represented the AL in 1996, 1998, 1999, 2000 and 2001.

The actual World Series was a banger, with four of the seven games between the Angels and Giants decided by just one run. To make that happen in Game 6, the Angels needed a six-run rally punctuated by Scott Spiezio's huge three-run homer .

Every year, there's a team that gets into October and gives off a sort of "Just lucky to be there" energy. More often than not, teams like those go nowhere.

Every now and then, though, you get a 2003 Marlins squad.

Though they managed to sneak into the playoffs via a wild card berth, they were widely expected to get bounced by a Giants squad that had won 100 games and which still featured Barry Bonds at the height of his power. That's not what happened, in large part because the Marlins held Bonds to just two hits in the NLDS.

Then came the Cubs series, which is certainly more famous for the fact that the Cubs lost . But just so everyone's clear, they didn't blow Game 6 because of that one fan . They lost that one because the Marlins put on a relentless eight-run rally that continued into Game 7, which they won 9-6.

Along the way, we got to know a young Miguel Cabrera as he hit three home runs in the playoffs. And we really got to know Josh Beckett, whose series-clinching shoutout in Game 6 of the World Series at Yankee Stadium should be the textbook definition of "stunned silence."

World Series: 4-3 vs. Kansas City Royals

The Giants won three World Series in the first half of the 2010s, and we won't argue with any Giants fans who say they prefer the run in 2010 or the run in 2012.

And yet, there's just something about the 2014 run that still gives off the feeling of pure madness. Maybe it's some residual disbelief that it was home runs by Joe Panik, Mike Morse and Travis Ishikawa that put the team in the World Series.

Or, maybe it's the still-radiating ridiculousness of the fact that Madison Bumgarner literally did that .

He pitched at least 7.0 innings in all six of his starts, bookended by shutouts in the NL Wild Card Game and in Game 5 of the World Series. That he followed the latter with 5.0 innings of shutout ball to save Game 7 just two days later is one of the great heroic feats in all of MLB history.

For Royals fans, that the 2014 World Series ended with Alex Gordon still on third base is one of the great "What if?" debates of recent memory. For Giants fans, all that matters is that Bumgarner left him stranded there.

The 2019 Nationals are what a team looks like when it refuses to go away.

They came back from 12 games under .500 during the regular season, and they eventually came from behind to win all three of their winner-take-all games in the postseason. And for those, the highlights are forever.

Anthony Rendon and Juan Soto going back-to-back off Clayton Kershaw to tie NLDS Game 5? Epic. Howie Kendrick's go-ahead grand slam in that game? Also epic. Rendon and Kendrick again in Game 7 of the World Series? So epic.

This was also, of course, the October of Stephen Strasburg. He became the first pitcher to ever go 5-0 in a single postseason, and he did so with a 1.98 ERA. He was the reason the Nats were even able to force a Game 7 in the World Series, as he came through with 8.1 innings of two-run ball when they faced elimination in Game 6.

To say that resulting triumph was a long time coming for the franchise would be understating it. Even if the first 35 years were in Montreal and not Washington D.C., it was still the Nationals' first World Series and championship in 50 years of trying.

Lest anyone forget, it took a miracle for the 2011 Cardinals just to get into the playoffs.

They had to erase an 8.5-game deficit, and the final act of that play didn't happen until a day of wild Game 162 action that still lives in baseball lore. Chris Carpenter pitched a two-hitter with 11 strikeouts to seal a wild-card berth, and that turned out to be a prologue of sorts.

Some of us can still picture it now. NLDS Game 5. Chris Carpenter vs. Roy Halladay. One pitches eight one-run innings and the other goes the distance and allows nothing. Final score: Cardinals 1, Phillies 0.

If the NLCS was relatively uneventful, the World Series most definitely was not. Albert Pujols homered three times in a Game 3 blowout, and Game 6 is rightfully counted among the best games of the century so far.

Josh Hamilton was clutch. Lance Berkman was clutch. David Freese was uber- clutch, both tying and winning Game 6 and ultimately finishing the postseason with 21 runs batted in. It was a record for a single October until Adolis García broke it in 2023.

This is the third of three World Series titles the Dodgers have won just since 2020, so perhaps there is some recency bias going on here.

What nobody will soon forget, though, is Shohei Ohtani having the greatest game ever by an individual player in Game 4 of the NLCS. A three-homer game is special. A 10-strikeout game is special. The two together is capital-I Insane .

As if that wasn't enough for Los Angeles and the entire nation of Japan to gloat over, Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched the first two complete games in the postseason since 2017 in NLCS Game 2 and World Series Game 2. He also became the first pitcher to win three World Series games since Randy Johnson in 2001.

The 2025 World Series otherwise featured two of the best games of the century, and the Dodgers won both of them. Freddie Freeman walked off Game 3 in the 18th inning. In Game 7, there was Andy Pages' catch , Miguel Rojas' game-tying shot * and Will Smith's winning shot .

*Just so it doesn't look like we're glossing over that… seriously, holy [bleep].

In the end, the Dodgers won a World Series that has a strong case as the best ever. And whether you love 'em or hate 'em, everyone should agree that they earned it.

Has it really been a quarter-century since the 2001 Diamondbacks stunned the world? More to the point, has it really been a quarter-century since Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling did that ?

For anyone who's too young to remember, you can basically imagine two guys each having a generational playoff run at the same time. Truly, Johnson and Schilling did not take a series off:

Their final tally? A total of 12 appearances and 89.2 innings, with a 1.30 ERA and 103 strikeouts against only 14 walks.

Though this largely explains how the 2001 D-backs triumphed over the Yankees, it took a team effort to overcome three successive gut punches in Games 3, 4 and 5 in New York. And even after all that, they ultimately faced the prospect of rallying against Mariano Rivera in Game 7.

Luis Gonzalez got all the glory for his walk-off bloop , and rightfully so. But please, do us all a favor and spread the word that Tony Womack's game-tying double was actually the more pivotal hit .

Even after 108 years of misery, the 2016 Cubs looked inevitable. Until they didn't. Then did again. Then didn't again.

Their regular season was a 103-win breeze, and they made relatively easy work of the Giants and Dodgers to get to the World Series. The closest they came to trouble was a 2-1 deficit to Los Angeles in the NLCS, but they then won three straight and outscored the Dodgers by 17 runs in the process.

The World Series? Different story. When they went down 3-1 to Cleveland, history was not on their side. No team had come back from 3-1 in the World Series since the Royals over the Cardinals in 1985.

What happened next is a story that Cubs fans will be telling to their kids and grandkids for a long time. Wins in Game 5 and 6. And then in Game 7, when they refused to let Rajai Davis' home run break them. To that end, Jason Heyward's mouth and Ben Zobrist's bat did the talking.

It was only the fourth World Series Game 7 to go into extra innings, and there was even a rain delay before the 10th inning started. But as any Cubs fan will tell you, after having to wait for 108 years, what's an extra hour or so as long as the W is flying in the end?

World Series: 4-0 vs. St. Louis Cardinals

What's worse than a 108-year wait for a World Series? How about an 86-year wait featuring too many heartbreaking close calls to count.

If you want to get technical, the Red Sox lost five seven-game series that went the distance between 1919 and 2003. There were World Series defeats in 1946, 1967, 1975 and 1986. There was also the 2003 ALCS, which followed the usual script of the Red Sox snatching defeat from the jaws of victory.

All that history was not just front and center, but mocking the Red Sox when they went down to the Yankees 3-0 in the 2004 ALCS. It was a death sentence, as no team had ever before erased that kind of deficit in an MLB playoff series.

Instead, heroes arrived as if out of those portals in Avengers: Endgame . Dave Roberts with the stolen base . David Ortiz with the walk-offs in Game 4 and Game 5 . Curt Schilling with the bloody sock . Johnny Damon with the grand slam .

After all that led to the Yankees' demise in the ALCS, actually winning the World Series felt like a formality. For history's sake, all that matters is that the Red Sox got it done to officially turn the "Curse of the Bambino" into history.

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: MLB Free Agents 2026 Predictions for Top Batters Set to Hit Open Market
articles.summary: In less than a week, a dozen fortunate MLB franchises will shift into their World Series-chasing playoff modes.
articles.body:
In less than a week, a dozen fortunate MLB franchises will shift into their World Series-chasing playoff modes.

For the less fortunate members of the baseball world, though, their focus may have already turned toward the hot stove.

Since a dozen-ish teams have already been eliminated from postseason contention, they might already be making offseason plans. A big part of that process may involve identifying potential upgrades to their lineup, and a select group of free agent hitters can help make that happen.

Let's break out the crystal ball, then, and determine where three of the biggest bats in free agency will eventually land.

The 2026 season wasn't Arozarena's first as an MLB All-Star (he had twice been selected before), but it may have been when his star shined brightest. And it couldn't have happened at a more opportune time with free agency awaiting him this offseason.

His bat perked up in ways it never had since becoming a full-time player. All three layers of his .279/.379/.480 slash line hit high marks for any season in which he played more than 25 games. His career-high 106 runs are the most in the American League. His 26 homers are one off his previous personal-best, and he tallied 20-plus steals for the sixth consecutive campaign.

Those are difference-making numbers, so his representation will surely hope the market winds up treating him as a difference-maker as a result. Time only knows if that will actually happen, but at least he started the conversation.

If he wants out of the less-than-hitter-friendly confines of Seattle's T-Mobile Park, he could have a host of outfield-needy suitors along the East Coast. The Boston Red Sox could certainly use his bat, but he'd be such a clear plug-and-play fit for the Atlanta Braves that our crystal ball sees them placing the highest bid.

Prediction: Arozarena signs a three-year deal with Atlanta.

When the Pirates tried making a push for the playoffs last offseason, they made the acquisition of Lowe a big part of that plan. While other elements of the strategy failed to come together, that one absolutely hit.

The 2026 season may go down as the best of the 32-year-old's career. His 5.2 WAR is the highest he has ever posted, per Baseball-Reference, while his 33 homers, 93 RBI and 92 runs are all the second-best of his career. That WAR is a testament to his dramatically improved defense, too.

He has even managed to quiet some of the old concerns with his availability. The 134 games he played last season ranked second on his career list, and they've subsequently been passed by his 146 appearances (and counting) this time around.

While it can be hard for a true second baseman to get paid, Lowe's prolific power could make him an exception to the rule. That probably isn't great news for the typically budget-conscious Pirates, but it should mean great things for Lowe, who might fetch an average annual salary at (or even north of) $25 million.

Prediction: Lowe signs a three-year deal with the New York Yankees.

Since arriving stateside in 2022, Suzuki has played a key role in anchoring Chicago's lineup. Utilized as both an outfielder and DH, he has delivered at least 20 home runs and 73 RBI in each of the last four seasons.

That kind of consistency should treat him well in free agency. Even if he's never had a true superstar spike—he arguably came closest last season, when he delivered 32 homers and knocked in 103 runs—he has been a generally productive hitter with near-star numbers. And his defense has never been better.

A lot of teams can use what he brings, including the Cubs. But with his contract value perhaps reaching nine figures, Chicago could choose to invest those funds elsewhere.

Offense-needy suitors will surely hope that's the case. With Seattle losing Arozarena in our projections, the Mariners might make Suzuki a priority and keep another power bat in their outfield.

Prediction: Suzuki signs a four-year deal with Seattle.

articles.title: Yoenis Cespedes Jr. Showcases Swing in Training Video Amid Rumors Interest from 'Several' MLB Teams
articles.summary: Yoenis Céspedes Jr., the 17-year-old son of the former MLB All-Star, could be following in his father's footsteps on a path to professional baseball.
articles.body:
Yoenis Céspedes Jr., the 17-year-old son of the former MLB All-Star, could be following in his father's footsteps on a path to professional baseball.

MLB insider Francys Romero posted video of Céspedes working out in the Dominican Republic where he trains at the Chiqui Mejias Academy and showing off his power.

In his Beisbol FR Substack newsletter, Romero noted the Atlanta Braves and San Diego Padres are among the MLB clubs monitoring Céspedes' progress recently.

Romero previously noted in December 2025 that scouts praised Céspedes' "bat skills, particularly his ability to recognize pitches and hit to all fields."

At just 17 years old, Céspedes is still growing into his frame but his power is starting to show in both batting practice and games. He can play either third base or a corner outfield position, but the bat is his primary selling point.

Céspedes comes from a strong athletic background. His father, Yoenis Céspedes, had a 16-year professional career between his time playing in Cuba and MLB.

The elder Céspedes spent eight seasons in MLB with four different teams. He finished second in AL Rookie of the Year voting to Mike Trout in 2012, hit at least 20 homers in each of his first five seasons and finished eighth in NL MVP in 2016 with the New York Mets.

Yoenis Céspedes Jr.'s grandparents were both athletes. Romero noted Céspedes' grandmother, Estela Milanés, was a pitcher for the Cuban national team that appeared in the 2000 Olympics.

Céspedes is currently eligible to sign with any MLB club.

articles.title: Meet Julio Rodriguez’s alter ego ‘DJ Pleno’: How the Seattle Mariners star is building a surprising second identity through house music, live sets and his growing passion for DJing
articles.summary: Discover how Seattle Mariners star Julio Rodriguez is reinventing himself as DJ Pleno, exploring his passion for house music and live performances.
articles.body: Seattle Mariners center fielder Julio Rodriguez is one of the most recognisable young faces in Major League Baseball with his energetic personality and impact on the field. But by 2026, Rodriguez is starting to be known for another facet of himself as he delves into music and live DJ sets.She goes by 'DJ Pleno' behind the turntables and is 25 years old. It’s a different identity from his baseball career, allowing Rodriguez to tinker with something that doesn’t have anything to do with the No. 44 jersey or his duties as a Mariners star. What began as a simple turntable in his home has now become a hobby that he wants to continue to build on.MLB star Julio Rodriguez introduces Seattle Mariners fans to DJ PlenoRodriguez’s DJ persona morphed from a private hobby to a public performance on August 7, 2026, at T-Mobile Park during the Seattle Mariners’ Alumni Home Run Derby. The event was part of the organization’s 50 Seasons Celebration Weekend and featured a number of former Mariners, including star attraction Ichiro Suzuki.But while the alumni were in the home run competition, Rodriguez had a different task. The Mariners star DJed live under the 'DJ Pleno' name, bringing house music to the ballpark after the game.The performance gave Rodriguez an opportunity to show a side of himself that most fans had not seen before. He was no longer in the batter’s box or patrolling center field he was in charge of music and trying to create an atmosphere for the crowd.To Rodriguez, the name 'Pleno' has meaning. The word has Spanish origins and is ultimately derived from Latin plēnus and ideas like being full, complete or fulfilled.That meaning helped Rodriguez find an identity that didn't revolve around baseball. Instead of opting for a name that referenced his number on his jersey, the Mariners or his baseball nickname, he wanted 'DJ Pleno' to be its own thing.The concept also reflects what Rodriguez wants to embody in the persona. He has associated the project with feeling good, being fulfilled and doing things that bring personal satisfaction in his comments around 'DJ Pleno'.The Alumni Home Run Derby performance was a big step forward because most of Rodriguez’s previous DJing had been done away from a large crowd.After the Mariners were knocked out of the playoffs in 2025, he began to tinker with equipment at his home in the Seattle area. His initial set-up was primitive, and Rodriguez admitted he had no idea what all the various controls on the equipment did.His friends who had DJ experience also made fun of his early equipment and method. Rodriguez did not give up the hobby but bought more equipment and kept on practising.How Julio Rodriguez discovered his passion for DJingRodriguez’s interest in DJing came during a period when he was looking for something outside of baseball. He’s been in the limelight since his teenage years, and his career has kept baseball front and center in his everyday life, from top prospect to established MLB star.DJing gives Rodriguez a different learning experienceRodriguez’s interest in music goes back a long way, but it was the decision to learn DJing that made it an active hobby. He bought a basic turntable and started practising at home after the 2025 season.There was an instant learning curve. Rodriguez said he initially had difficulty understanding the controls, but repeated practice helped him become more comfortable with the equipment and the process of mixing tracks.His musical preferences lie in house music and he is associated with artists such as Martin Garrix and Black Coffee. He doesn’t have a strict daily routine for DJing. Instead, Rodriguez likes to train when the mood is right.There’s an interesting link to Rodriguez’s baseball career and his new hobby. He has spent most of his life working on his baseball skills, so a lot of the game comes on instinct through years of repetition.As a novice, Rodriguez has to relearn the fundamentals, make mistakes and slowly improve. And that process has allowed him to think about his own development as a baseball player and to appreciate how much work went into getting to the major leagues.Rodriguez has likened the thrill of having control of a DJ set to the sensation of creating a big moment on a baseball field.If you’re a player accustomed to the decibel levels at T-Mobile Park, then playing music in front of a crowd isn’t all that foreign. The energy may be similar, but the source of attention is different.What comes next for Julio Rodriguez and DJ PlenoRodriguez has described 'DJ Pleno' as a work in progress. There doesn’t seem to be a concrete, long-term business plan for the project, but the Mariners star has said he’d like to continue to grow and eventually expand what he’s able to do with music.He wants to do more than just mix. Rodriguez has said he wants to do his own music in the future, which could see the project move from DJing to production.Next for Rodriguez is to get more confidence technically and gain more experience in front of audiences. The Alumni Home Run Derby was an important first major opportunity, but the center fielder has hinted there could be more performances to come.In August 2026, the singer-songwriter Ed Sheeran visited T-Mobile Park, and Rodriguez also discussed his DJing interest with him.Sheeran told Rodriguez to keep practicing and honing the skill, even if friends or others don’t immediately respond positively to the music. articles.title: Yordan Alvarez, Jacob Misiorowski, AL, NL Stat Leaders Ahead of 2026 MLB Season's Final Weekend
articles.summary: With five days remaining in the 2026 MLB regular season, the individual stats leaderboard is almost as unsettled as the playoff races in both leagues.
articles.body:
With five days remaining in the 2026 MLB regular season, the individual stats leaderboard is almost as unsettled as the playoff races in both leagues.

The key races going into the final weekend involve Yordan Alvarez's quest for the AL triple crown and Jacob Misiorowski looking to lead all of MLB in strikeouts.

Here are the leaders in several individual categories going into Wednesday's games.

Ranking MLB's 10 Greatest Postseason Runs Since 2000 🏆

Alvarez will need a strong close to the season to win the triple crown. He still leads the AL in average and is tied for the lead in homers, but his RBI pace has fallen off this month.

The Houston Astros star had just five RBI in his first 16 games in September before driving in three on Tuesday in a 7-0 win over the Seattle Mariners.

Alvarez is up to 102 RBI for the season. Pete Alonso's 17 RBI this month have pushed him up to 108 with five games remaining.

Alvarez and Luis Arraez are tied for the MLB lead with a .314 batting average. Both players look like safe bets to maintain that position through Sunday.

Misiorowski, the biggest breakout star of the season for the 2026 NL Central champion Milwaukee Brewers, is looking to become the first pitcher to lead MLB in both ERA and strikeouts in a 162-game season since Jake Peavy in 2007.

The MLB ERA title is down to Misiorowski at 1.86 and New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler at 1.94. Misiorowski will likely get one more abbreviated start in Milwaukee's final regular-season series against the St. Louis Cardinals.

Schlittler is scheduled to make his final regular-season start on Thursday against the Tampa Bay Rays. Since the Yankees are locked into the No. 4 seed, he is also likely to have a shortened outing to prepare for Game 1 of the wild-card round on Tuesday.

The strikeout race is arguably more compelling than the ERA title because Gavin Williams of the Cleveland Guardians will likely get the nod on Friday against the Kansas City Royals.

Since the Guardians can't wrap up the AL Central until Friday at the earliest, Williams will likely have a regular outing. He is currently only three Ks behind Misiorowski for the MLB lead.

Williams has 15 strikeouts in 11.2 innings against the Royals this season, but he hasn't faced them since May 5.

NL MVP favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong is one stolen base away from the seventh player in MLB history to have a 40-40 season. He can also become the first Chicago Cubs player to lead the NL in homers since Sammy Sosa hit 49 in 2002.

Five clubs could lock in a trip to the 2026 MLB postseason this Wednesday.

The Athletics, Cincinnati Reds, Colorado Rockies, Detroit Tigers, Kansas City Royals, Los Angeles Angels, Miami Marlins, Minnesota Twins, New York Mets, Pittsburgh Pirates, St. Louis Cardinals, San Francisco Giants and Washington Nationals have been eliminated from playoff contention.

The Cubs have the most possible ways to clinch after previously blowing an opportunity to secure a spot with a Tuesday night loss to the Miami Marlins.

Either a Wednesday redemption win over the Marlins or a Colorado Rockies win over the Arizona Diamondbacks will be enough to send the Cubs to the playoffs.

The outcome of the Rockies/Diamondbacks game could also impact a few other postseason hopefuls.

The White Sox need a victory over the Kansas City Royals combined with a New York Mets win over the Texas Rangers.

The Cleveland Guardians are looking for a win over the Red Sox, combined with either a Mets victory of a Houston Astros win over the Seattle Mariners.

The outcomes of the White Sox and Guardians games will also play a role in determining who wins the race to the top of the AL Central and potentially an AL top seed and Wild Card-round bye.

Whichever club wins the division will get the chance to secure both the bye and divisional home-field advantage if the Guardians beat the Red Sox, the Mariners defeat the Astros and the Mets win over the Rangers this Wednesday, per MLB.com's Andrew Simon .

articles.title: Max Scherzer Addresses Retirement Speculation Near End of 19th MLB Season
articles.summary: Everything is seemingly lined up for Max Scherzer to retire after his 19th season in Major League Baseball, but the Toronto Blue Jays pitcher isn't ready to say 2026 is his final year.
articles.body:
Everything is seemingly lined up for Max Scherzer to retire after his 19th season in Major League Baseball, but the Toronto Blue Jays pitcher isn't ready to say 2026 is his final year.

"I don't know if I want to publicly say, yet," he said Wednesday, per insider Hazel Mae . "I'd rather keep the blinders up and address once the season's over. … I'm not limping to the finish line, I'm accelerating through the finish line. … Want to keep the focus on just getting to the finish line."

Scherzer is 42 years old, already has a Hall of Fame resume and is playing in the final season of his contract with the Blue Jays. It certainly wouldn't be a surprise if he called it a career when the 2026 campaign ends.

Still, he has been solid of late and allowed three or fewer earned runs in four of his last five starts. One of those starts came against the Seattle Mariners on Aug. 30 when he allowed a single hit and no earned runs with 10 strikeouts in seven innings of work.

It was a turn-back-the-clock performance for the three-time Cy Young winner.

While Scherzer is correct that he isn't "limping to the finish line," his season-long numbers are far from his peak. He has a 6.07 ERA, 1.36 WHIP and 54 strikeouts in 72.2 innings after posting a 5.19 ERA last season.

That is a far cry from his 3.28 career ERA that helped him build a resume that includes those Cy Youngs, two World Series titles and eight All-Star selections.

Scherzer will end up in Cooperstown after he retires, but his performances of late suggest he may be able to help a team next season if decides against retirement.

For now, he is focused on finishing the 2026 season with a Blue Jays team that is four games out of the final American League Wild Card spot with five games remaining.

articles.title: Nationals' Cade Cavalli Shields Part of New Contract from Potential MLB Lockout
articles.summary: Details have emerged about Washington Nationals starting pitcher Cade Cavalli's new four-year, $47 million contract, initially revealed last Friday.

Details have emerged about Washington Nationals starting pitcher Cade Cavalli's new four-year, $47 million contract, initially revealed last Friday.

Notably, the Associated Press reported that on Nov. 30, Cavalli will receive a $4 million signing bonus, which the AP described as "a payment shielded from potential losses caused by a possible lockout" in the 2027 season.

The AP noted Cavalli's salaries will be $4 million (2027), $7 million (2028), $10 million (2029) and $20 million (2030). The Nats have an option in 2031 to keep Cavalli aboard for $25 million or buy out that season for $2 million.

Ranking MLB's 10 Greatest Postseason Runs Since 2000 🏆

The 28-year-old Cavalli went 13-5 with a 3.02 ERA (1.155 WHIP) over 32 starts (169.2 innings) this season. He also struck out 200 batters.

Cavalli's final appearance was on Friday, when he threw five shutout innings and struck out six in a 9-1 win over the St. Louis Cardinals. He's now done for the season, per Spencer Nusbaum of The Athletic, who explained why.

Cavalli was the Nationals' top starter this year, and he's in line to be the team's ace this year.

Of course, there's much concern about the status of the 2027 season since the current Major League Baseball collective bargaining agreement will expire on December 1 if a new agreement isn't reached.

Per an ESPN report on Sept. 2, owners' insistence on instituting a salary cap (and players' resistance to one) is the biggest issue, to the point that some players interviewed anonymously have concerns about whether teams will play all 162 games.

As of now, a full schedule is on the table for 2027, but Cavalli's contract has a safeguard in place for the starting pitcher in case time is missed.

articles.title: Aaron Judge's wild-card absence offers a glimpse of a rapidly approaching Yankees future
articles.summary: Entering October without a world-beating Judge is a bizarre new reality — and also one the Yankees might need to get familiar with.
articles.body:
Their doubleheader split with the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday ensured that the Bombers will enter the postseason as the top wild card in the American League . (The Rays clinched the AL East and the No. 1 seed ). That means, barring a major surprise over the next few days, New York is set to host its forever rivals , the Boston Red Sox , in a best-of-three series starting Tuesday in the Bronx.

But while the schedule and the opponent offer a dose of certainty, there's one enormous unknown swirling around YankeeLand: the health of three-time MVP Aaron Judge .

It has been an injury-riddled season for the Yankees' captain, who missed more than three months due to a stress fracture on his first rib. He returned Sept. 8 and appeared in seven games, tallying four hits and one homer, before landing back on the shelf due to a calf strain suffered Sept. 16. Predictably, the Yankees have been quite mum about Judge's status. Skipper Aaron Boone first declined to disclose the severity of the strain but eventually described it as "moderate." Judge has not spoken publicly since the calf situation flared up and he was removed midgame.

But before Tuesday's doubleheader, Boone told reporters that Judge won't return during the regular season and that the Yankees are "planning on him not being a part" of the team's wild-card exploits. While that doesn't entirely close the door on a heroic comeback from the goliath slugger, all signs point toward Judge taking in October's opening act from the dugout.

In the event that he does return next week, it's difficult to envision Judge doing so at full strength. Notably, the calf issue is on his right leg — his rear or plant leg. Judge's swing mechanics are particularly reliant on his having explosiveness and stability in his right hip and right leg. Without that, he could be a shell of his best self. Still, players are famously more willing to use certain medications and numbing agents in the postseason, things that could help push Judge onto the roster.

His not being able to play in the outfield is another consideration. Even after the lengthy layoff, Judge slotted immediately back into right field, in part because the Yankees' roster is overloaded with designated hitter types. A more cautious course of action might've saved Judge's calf from giving out, though it's impossible to know for sure.

But now, given the glut of DHs on New York 's roster, it's hard to imagine a super-reduced version of Judge being the optimal choice in the lineup over Ben Rice or Paul Goldschmidt . As such, how Boone slots Judge back into the mix if the Yankees journey deep into the playoffs will be one of the more fascinating storylines to follow.

Until then, the Yanks will need to soldier on, a man — one very large man — down.

This era of Yankees baseball has simultaneously been shaped by Judge and shaped around him. Critics have argued the current roster is overly dependent on the future Hall of Famer — a ridiculous proposition. Wouldn't anyone build a team around one of the world's best hitters? Still, entering October without a world-beating Judge is a bizarre new reality and, at the same time, one the Yankees, given Judge's age, might need to acquaint themselves with.

New York has not played a postseason contest without Judge since the 2015 winner-take-all wild-card game. A 40-year-old Alex Rodriguez hit fourth for the Yanks that day. Dallas Keuchel threw six shutout innings for a plucky, likable Houston Astros team yet to villainize themselves in the baseball world. Colby Rasmus and Carlos Gómez each ripped solo homers in Houston's victory. Since then, Judge has appeared in all 65 of New York's playoff games, the most over that span by a non-Dodger or non-Astro.

Of course, Judge's physical woes this season do not necessarily portend the beginning of the end. Playing through pain and in a small sample, the 6-foot-7 Californian still posted an impressive .871 OPS. He was, less than a year ago, the American League MVP. He surely has more magical moments to conjure, more souvenirs to crank into the seats. And yet, the clock is undeniably ticking. Father Time, you see, has never been defeated.

The Yankees' captain will turn 35 in April. There have been only 22 individual MLB seasons since integration (1947) in which a qualified player 35 or older finished with an OPS over 1.000. Seven of those years — five from Barry Bonds, one from Mark McGwire and one from Manny Ramírez — were likely aided by performance enhancers. The list, understandably, grows only smaller as the age ticks closer to 40. It's hard to be elite; it's even harder as your body decays.

Judge could certainly ward off Father Time and his sinister ways and remain otherworldly for a few more years. Ted Williams did it. So did Henry Aaron and Chipper Jones and David Ortiz . Some folks age like fine wine. Judge is disciplined, driven and athletic enough to make it work. Modern medical and training technology make it easier for the best to stay healthy for longer. Nobody would be shocked if Judge has another MVP season in him.

But the opposite is also true. Even if his production doesn't tumble off a cliff, there's reason to be wary about the future. Judge cannot carry this franchise around on his broad shoulders forever. Eventually, the Yankees will need to pivot, grow, change, chart a new course. And given the club's institutional smarts and financial might, chances are they'll find another aircraft carrier on which to center the franchise.

Besides, the Yankees' pitching-driven success this year is a reminder that such a path is possible, even fruitful. The 2026 New York Yankees have won a lot of games without Judge. They might need to continue doing so in October.

articles.title: Carl Junction Bulldogs blank Hillcrest 16-0
articles.summary: CARL JUNCTION, Mo. — Carl Junction High School's softball team plated 16 runs in the second inning en route to a three-inning run-rule win over the Hillcrest...
articles.body:
CARL JUNCTION, Mo. — Carl Junction High School's softball team plated 16 runs in the second inning en route to a three-inning run-rule win over the Hillcrest High School Hornets (2-11) Tuesday at CJHS.

Senior Jazmyne Blayney went 2 for 2 with five RBIs and two runs and hit a three-run homer in the Bulldogs' explosive second frame to lead CJ hitters.

Three other Bulldogs logged multiple hits in the game. Pitcher Aubrey Lisenbee was 2 for 2 with two RBIs and two runs and Kenleigh Palmer and Kinley Spindler both finished 2 for 3 with two RBIs and two runs each.

CJ (7-9) also ran rampant on the base paths, with nine stolen bases. Kady Hunt had three and Palmer finished with two.

"We like to be aggressive on the base paths," CJ head coach Mandy Bauer said. "Tonight, we took advantage of them (Hillcrest) not covering the bag and got runners in scoring position. We have a big game Thursday night against Bolivar, so we wanted to make sure we were practicing base running when we had the opportunity in certain situations."

The Bulldogs got on the board in the bottom of the second frame when Lisenbee drove in Braylen Johnson with a line drive single to left field.

Spindler made it a 3-0 game when she plated Lisenbee and Addi Gau with a single to center. A Palmer bunt scored Spindler, and Blayney increased the CJ lead to 6-0 with a line drive to left that brought Palmer and Hunt across the plate.

Blayney later scored on a wild pitch, Johnson drove in Gracie Arnold with a double to left field and Lisenbee made it 9-0 when she played Johnson with a liner to center field.

The CJ lead mushroomed to 12-0 when Gau doubled to left field and, after two Hillcrest errors, Lisenbee, Christy Marney and Gau all scored. Palmer then drove in Spindler.

Blayney put the icing on the cake for CJ with a three-run line drive over the center field fence that scored Palmer and Hunt and gave the Bulldogs a 16-0 lead.

"Jazmyne is a great kid. She has been on the struggle bus, so I really wanted her to have that at-bat so she could maybe get a big hit like she did and get back on the right path," Bauer said. "We've all kind of been on the struggle bus lately, but this week we understood the assignment and got back to work."

Blayney was succinct when asked about her homer.

"That was me, and that was my damage," Blayney said of the at-bat.

Lisenbee gave up one hit and no runs, while striking out four and walking none in two innings of work. She logged the win after hurling just 20 pitches.

CJ travels to Bolivar High School (11-5) for a 4:30 p.m. game Thursday and returns home to face Carthage High School (7-14) at 4:30 p.m. Monday.
authors: Laurie Sisk, The Joplin Globe, Mo.

Tonight, they have one of their best arms on the hill as the Mets send out Nolan McLean to the hill in hopes of ending his year with a strong final start. He has been great on the road this season with a 2.89 ERA and holding opposing hitters to batting just .197. The Rangers haven't faced McLean much in his career, hitting just 2-for-10 against him. METS FIRE CARLOS MENDOZA AMID NIGHTMARE SEASON DESPITE HAVING BASEBALL'S LARGEST $330M PAYROLL The Texas Rangers are still trying to fight for the American League West. They are fighting for the top spot with the Astros, and they are currently tied for the division lead. Whoever loses is also not assured of a playoff spot, as they are chasing the White Sox in that race as well. The Rangers have picked a bad time to lose some games as they've dropped the past two games, including the opener against the Mets. Now they need to figure out the way to win and stay alive. The Rangers have one simple mission: win to get in. In hopes of getting there, they trade Cody Bradford. For the season, Bradford is 0-5 with a 4.19 ERA and a 1.50 WHIP. He has been better at home this year than on the road, sporting a 3.50 ERA over just four games played. He has only appeared in eight games, but the Rangers are 1-7 in the games he has played. He has not faced the Mets this season and has only faced Mets hitters seven times over his career, and they are 2-for-7 against him. I'm not sure how you can back Texas in this spot. The Rangers are not playing great baseball, even if they need to play it right now. Bradford has been fine overall, but the Rangers haven't given him much support. I'm going to take the Mets and McLean today, as I think he positions himself better for the win. Give me the Mets moneyline.
